A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ShEPhERD work. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching retained material across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original molecular-generation experiments, similarity and validity measurements, docking evaluations, natural-product ligand hopping and fragment merging, with additional results in the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds further ShEPhERD evaluations and baseline comparisons in Appendix A.12. Some comparator scores are explicitly attributed to prior publications.

M1.justification: The representations, denoising architecture, objectives and sampling algorithms are retained. Shape-only conditioning in A.12.1 uses the existing inpainting procedure: Algorithm 5 already permits conditioning on arbitrary subsets of interaction-profile variables.

E1.justification: A.12.3 adds the 4tos protein–ligand case, using ligand 355 with 42 non-hydrogen atoms, beyond the original seven docking targets. The training datasets, three natural-product examples and fragment-merging system remain unchanged; coverage expands within the existing drug-design domain.

E2.justification: A.12 adds comparisons with SQUID, ShapeMol/ShapeMol+g, 3DSBDD, AutoGrow4, Pocket2Mol, PocketFlow, ResGen, DiffSBDD and SynFormer. SQUID and DiffSBDD outputs are re-evaluated, and SynFormer is run; ShapeMol and the five Table 11 SBDD baselines use published scores. These substantially extend v1's evaluated comparator set.

E3.justification: The added comparisons introduce substantial evaluation protocols: shape-only conditioning on 1,000 MOSES test molecules with up to ten samples per target and ROCS scoring; up to 1,000 valid molecules per target for Table 11; 100 valid molecules per method with Vina 1.1.2 for 4tos; and up to ten xTB-optimized conformers per SynFormer analogue. These supplement the retained experimental settings.

E4.justification: A.1.1 and Figure 6 add REINVENT convergence diagnostics and synthetic-accessibility distributions. Figures 31–32 add graph-similarity analyses of generated ligands. These focused diagnostics supplement the unchanged validity, symmetry-breaking and out-of-distribution analyses; Figure 10 separately visualizes existing docking examples.

E5.justification: Existing seed disclosures, fivefold surface-resampling analysis and mean/dispersion reporting are retained. The new tables extend dispersion reporting to additional results without introducing new repeated-run counts, confidence intervals or significance-testing procedures.

E6.justification: Tables 10–11 and Figures 31–34 add substantial results. Table 10 reports shape similarity of 0.799 for ShEPhERD versus 0.700/0.735 for SQUID, alongside lower ShEPhERD QED. New docking and SynFormer comparisons provide further outcomes under their stated settings. Original result displays are retained, while Section 4 softens the specific '5/7' docking summary to 'multiple cases'.

T1.justification: The mathematical representations, similarity definitions, diffusion equations and appendix derivations are retained. Notation and typesetting adjustments do not change the mathematical reasoning, and no new theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution statements and conclusion retain the same claims about joint interaction-aware diffusion, similarity scoring and the three bioisosteric design applications. Added comparisons support these contributions without redefining their scope.

C2.justification: v2 acknowledges incomplete REINVENT convergence and qualifies the new comparisons through differences in conditioning information, ShapeMol alignment protocols and SynFormer's objective. A.12 interprets docking results as evidence of SBDD potential while recognizing comparison limitations. The original mechanism explanations and applicability arguments remain.

D1.justification: A.12 documents baseline-output provenance, the all-atom DiffSBDD inpainting variant, Vina 1.1.2 and SynFormer conformer handling. A.1.1 adds that REINVENT evaluation required multiple days per target. Existing architecture hyperparameters, training resources, algorithms and code/data access statements are retained.

R1.justification: Gao et al. (2024), introducing SynFormer, is added to the references. A.12 expands discussion of ShEPhERD's relationship to shape-conditioned, pocket-conditioned and synthesis-oriented generators. The main related-work section and central novelty positioning remain largely unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 adds A.1.1 and A.12, makes limited sampling and docking prose edits, and updates author affiliations, acknowledgments and the conference header. The original section sequence and most existing prose remain intact rather than undergoing extensive rewriting.

P2.justification: v2 adds a substantial set of comparative and diagnostic displays: Tables 10–11, convergence and accessibility plots, graph-similarity histograms, and DiffSBDD/SynFormer comparison figures. Figure 10 separately displays docking poses already represented in Figure 4. Existing figures and tables are otherwise retained, with relocation and renumbering.

improvement.justification: v1 relied mainly on random/virtual screening and REINVENT comparisons, leaving evaluation against other 3D generators limited. Table 10's SQUID comparison using the same MOSES split addresses that important gap. Additional docking comparisons and convergence diagnostics strengthen comparative validation and transparency. Unequal conditioning, imported baseline scores and SynFormer's different objective limit some comparisons, but these limitations are largely disclosed and do not outweigh the substantial evidential gain.
